fields.meta_title: Salon Booking Form Builder for Hair Salons | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a salon booking form that books each service for its real length, prices it by stylist level, and saves every booking. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Salon Booking Form That Fits Every Service Length
fields.hero_description: Build a salon booking form that offers only the times a service fits, at each stylist's price, saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Knows About Each Salon Chair
fields.features_subheading: A salon booking form books time out of a stylist's day. Emergent builds the form and the schedule it checks before a time appears.
fields.feature_1:
Start times that fit the whole service

Give every service its length, such as 95 minutes for root color. The form shows a start time only when the stylist has that full length free. No service runs into the next client's.
fields.feature_2:
Color processing opens a short slot

Split each color service into application, processing, and finish. While the color sets, the stylist's hands are free, and the form offers that window to a cut that fits inside it.
fields.feature_3:
Prices and times set by stylist level

Set a price and a length for each service at every stylist level. Clients see both beside each stylist's name before they pick, and the booking keeps the price they were shown.
fields.feature_4:
One request books a whole group

A wedding party books in one request. The organizer enters a head count and a ready-by time, and the form spreads the services across free stylists. Everyone is done by that time.
fields.feature_5:
A day view for the front desk

The app gives the front desk one screen with every stylist's day, processing windows included. A walk-in client gets a time from the same schedule the booking form reads from.
fields.feature_6:
Your salon's code, exported to GitHub

Paid plans export the whole codebase to your GitHub repository, where a developer can extend the form later. Bookings sit in a database you own, and no response cap limits them.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Salons, Four Ways to Book a Chair
fields.tab_content_1:
With Ysabeau's color setting, a 10:30 cut goes to Stellan

Root color at Ombrelle Hair Studio takes 95 minutes, and 35 of them are processing time. Ysabeau Cosgrave books it with Orsolya Zelinski for 10 a.m. Orsolya applies the color until 10:30, and the form opens 10:30 to 11:05 for short services. Stellan Ellingham books a 30-minute cut in that window.
fields.tab_content_2:
Elodie charges $52 and Maelle $88 for the same cut

Gilded Shear Salon prices every service by stylist level. A women's cut is $52 and 60 minutes with Elodie Thackery at Level 1, or $88 and 45 minutes with Maelle Dunstan at Level 3. Briallen Corvaja sees both before she picks Elodie's Thursday 4 p.m. opening, and the form books the full 60 minutes.
fields.tab_content_3:
Five updos on two chairs, all done at 9:45 a.m.

Margit Oyelaran needs hair for 5 people at Cinderwell Salon on her wedding day, ready by 10 a.m. Each updo takes 45 minutes, and the form works back from the ready-by time. It gives 3 updos to one stylist and 2 to another, both starting at 7:30 a.m. The last one finishes at 9:45. Every guest gets her own start time.
fields.tab_content_4:
Anselm's next cut is booked from one email

Corbel Row Salon emails each client 6 weeks after a cut. Anselm Vearey had his with Cassia Penhallow on March 3, so on April 14 the app emails him a link to Cassia's open times. He uses it to book April 18 at 5:30 p.m. The new booking lands on his client record under the March 3 visit.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Salon Booking Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a salon booking form that books every service for its real length, built and tested with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Time every service on your menu
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Mark where color sits and processes
fields.howto_step_1_des: Go through the menu and put a length next to each service: 95 minutes for root color, 30 for a men's cut, 45 for an updo. Pad the services newer stylists take longer on. The form reads these lengths whenever it lists start times.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down how long each color service spends being applied, processing, and finished, such as 30, 35, and 30 minutes for root color. The stylist's hands are free during the middle block. Say which short services may be booked into it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Assign every stylist a level, then decide what each service costs and how long it runs at that level. A newer stylist might need 60 minutes for a cut a senior stylist finishes in 45. Clients see both numbers before they choose who to book.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the largest party you take in one request and the earliest hour you will open the salon for it. Ask the organizer how many people are coming and when they must be ready. The form splits the group across free stylists and works back to a start.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the service menu, the color timings, the stylist levels, and the group rules into one prompt. Emergent builds the salon booking form, the database every booking lands in, and a schedule screen for the front desk. Change any rule later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose how long after each service a client should hear from you, such as 6 weeks after a cut. The app emails a link to the same stylist's open times. A booking made from that link is saved on the client's record next to the last visit.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Book a color client as a test
fields.howto_step_7_des: Book root color for 10 a.m. tomorrow under a test name. Then try to book a 30-minute cut with the same stylist at 10:30. It should go through, and both bookings should appear on the front desk's schedule with the processing time marked.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a salon booking form for my hair studio where clients pick a service, a stylist, and an open time.

faq_plan.q: What is a salon booking form?
faq_plan.a: A salon booking form is the page a client uses to book a salon appointment. They pick a service, a stylist, and a start time. Then they leave a name and a phone number. Behind it, the form reads each stylist's day and offers only the times the service fits.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a salon booking form?
faq_plan.a: Write down your services with their lengths, your stylists and their levels, and any rules for color or groups. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, which builds the form and the database behind it. Book a few test appointments yourself before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What should a salon booking form ask for?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the client's name and phone, the service, the stylist, and the start time. Move color history and allergy questions to a separate form at check-in, and keep booking short. Add an email field only if you plan to send confirmations or reminders by email.

faq_plan.q: How should a salon booking form handle a wedding party?
faq_plan.a: Take the whole party in one request from the organizer, with a guest list rather than five separate bookings. Ask for each guest's name and service. A guest who only needs makeup then never holds a hair chair. An event booking form is the better fit when guests share one start time, such as a class at your salon.

faq_plan.q: How does a salon booking form avoid double-booking a stylist?
faq_plan.a: Have the form check the stylist's schedule before it lists a time, and offer only starts where the whole service fits. Book walk-ins and phone appointments into the same schedule the form reads. A time taken at the front desk then drops off the form.

faq_plan.q: Should a salon booking form show prices?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Show each service's price next to the stylist who offers it, especially when prices change with stylist level. Save the price on the booking to make the total at the front desk match what the client saw. Emergent keeps every booking in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I add color processing time to a salon booking form?
faq_plan.a: Set the processing minutes on each color service and list the services that can be booked inside them. Pick services shorter than the processing window. A 30-minute cut fits a 35-minute window with time left to check the color. The same split suits any booking form for a service with a waiting stage in the middle.

faq_plan.q: Can a salon booking form send appointment reminders?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The app can email each client the day before with the time and the stylist, plus a link to change the booking. It can also send the stylist an in-app alert when a new booking lands. Emergent builds these from the same prompt that describes the form.

faq_plan.q: How far ahead should a salon booking form let clients book?
faq_plan.a: Match it to how far ahead your stylists set their schedules, such as 8 weeks. A longer window lets regulars hold their next cut before they leave the chair, and a shorter one keeps time open for new clients. Change the window later by asking Emergent in plain English.

faq_plan.q: Can a salon booking form book hair and nail services together?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each service the staff and the station it needs, such as a stylist's chair or a pedicure chair, and offer a time only when both are free. A hotel booking form counts rooms by the night, while a salon form counts chairs and staff by the minute.
